articles.title: How Glenn Schumann can fix FSU football recruiting in Florida, Georgia
articles.summary: Here's why the Florida State football hiring of Glenn Schumann may be just what the Seminoles need to reclaim recruiting strength near home.
articles.body:
The head coach saga in Tallahassee appears to be over (although anything is possible in college sports ), and the Glenn Schumann era is underway at Florida State football .

Schumann has a tough assignment ahead of him . Leading one of the nation's best defense in the middle of a championship-level season is tough enough, but accepting a new gig opens the door to a new world of challenges. If that gig happens to be Florida State in 2026 , it's less of a door and more Pandora's box.

Meet Glenn Schumann, FSU football's next head coach

While Schumann directs the Bulldog defense, an anxious Seminole fanbase awaits his arrival. Among the questions for Schumann is can he boost FSU's recruiting, which currently holds the No. 58 class in the nation for the class of 2027 , according to 247Sports.. The class took an enormous hit after four-star prospect Za'Karri Johnson reclassified back to his original class of 2028, joining fellow south Florida 'Nole commit and former teammate at Cypress Bay, EDGE Meshi Dobson, who had done the same earlier this year.

Florida State has some good players in this class, but it's a far cry from the standard established in Tallahassee. Without Dobson and Johnson, the 'Noles hold just three commits in the USA TODAY Florida Top 100 — the same number as North Carolina, two less than Pitt and four less than Florida.

Schumann's first step, when he gets the chance, will to be to look at the class as currently constructed. Some players may not fit the need, fit, or price tag for the new staff. Florida State has also extended offers since Norvell has been fired, and the new staff may not be inclined to honor them.

Additionally, who will be on the new coaching staff, and whom will they recruit? We see players follow coaches all the time, and Florida State is the type of program that can vie for elite players. If Schumann is bringing aboard key names from power programs, some late four- or five-star additions are not impossible. With the Norvell cloud gone in Tallahassee and replaced with Schumann's track record, the pitch just got a lot stronger. This is especially true for the elite recruiters already on campus like Tim Harris Jr., Nick Williams, and Ernie Sims.

All of these are important questions for Schumann, and we'll find out more in time. But what we do know for now is that Schumann brings an immediate recruiting boost to Tallahassee.

Why Georgia should be on their minds for FSU football

The 'Noles supplemented recruiting losses in their home state with wins for recruits from Georgia in recent years. Historically, Florida State has had few issues recruiting the Peach State and has even been a recruiting powerhouse in the state.

Under Schumann, expect that pipeline to expand. He's a proven winner in his home state and is as respected a recruiter as they come in the prep ranks. The 'Nole logo shines brightly in the hotbed that is south Georgia, and he will likely flex it strongly in the 2028 cycle and beyond.

Schumann is by no means a stranger to his new home state, either. Some of Schumann's first big recruiting wins were in the Sunshine State, starting with scooping up four-star DL Bear Alexander and five-star EDGE Daylen Everette from IMG, plus five-star CB Marvin Jones Jr. out of Fort Lauderdale.

In his second year, he took five-star LB Raylen Wilson out of Tallahassee, and then flipped five-star DL Jordan Hall out of Jacksonville away from Florida. All he has done since is pluck elite defensive players from talent factories like IMG and St. Thomas Aquinas in Florida while raiding Georgia's powerhouse prep programs.

FSU's recruiting class of 2027 may ultimately be something a defensive coach loves to see — a punt. One would think Georgia's expectations take Schumann's responsibilities well past the early signing period Dec. 2-4, and he has a lot to figure out before turning to a class he has less than a month to finalize.

Florida head coach Jon Sumrall was in a similar position last year , coming over from Tulane and largely kept a strong class intact. Nobody was expecting Tulane to make a deep run in the College Football Playoff like Schumann's Georgia squad, however, and adding to the class will be easier said than done.

Once Schumann is permanently in Tallahassee with his staff intact, the 'Noles will be in a great spot on the recruiting trail. Fans just need to let him get there first.

articles.body:

articles.title: College football risers and fallers: UCLA, Indiana trending down with CFP hopes in flux
articles.summary: UCLA and Indiana lead our risers and fallers after Week 12 of the college football season.
articles.body:
Indiana and UCLA both dropped games against unranked Washington and Michigan, respectively, in Week 12, putting a dent in both of their College Football Playoff hopes.

Uncertainty regarding both teams' CFP cases leads USA TODAY Sports' latest risers and fallers ahead of the final week of the regular season.

The Hoosiers and Bruins are still in contention for a 12-team playoff berth nonetheless, but the path is less clear than it was before their pair of losses, especially with six teams still alive in the Big Ten championship game hunt, which will grant one team an automatic berth.

Their losses have opened the door for Oregon, which has fought back into the CFP discussion with backup quarterback Dylan Raiola after a slow start to the season and a disastrous game after Dante Moore was hurt against USC.

Here's a look at which teams are trending up and down after Week 12:

A loss to LSU would've put Tennessee in a tough spot regarding its CFP chances. The Vols aren't leaving any doubts about their case, though, with a 27-13 win over the Tigers.

Tennessee has had its fair share of doubters this season but has found a formula to winning as of late despite mostly poor quarterback play between a pair of first-year starters in George MacIntyre and Faizon Brandon. Running back DeSean Bishop, a finalist for the Doak Walker Award, has carried the load for the Vols' run-heavy offense.

Tennessee finishes its regular season against Vanderbilt, a game it should win to lock up a 10-2 season and a potential CFP first-round game at home.

Oregon was expected to be one of the top national championship contenders this season, but was upset by Oklahoma State in nonconference play before losing two of its first four Big Ten games to UCLA and Illinois.

The Ducks have found something since, however, with four consecutive wins — the last three by double-digits — against Northwestern, Ohio State, Michigan and Michigan State. They've positioned themselves for a potential Big Ten championship game appearance and maybe even an at-large CFP bid despite all the ups and downs of this season.

It seems unlikely right now, but if Oregon was able to sneak into the CFP, it's not a team most opponents would be happy to see.

Utah is the only team left in FBS with an undefeated record. The Utes have faced some adversity the last few weeks against Arizona and TCU, but have found a way to win games, which is what good teams do.

Utah has virtually locked up a CFP berth and will likely face Texas Tech in the Big 12 championship game, which the Utes have also already made. Utah has ranked wins over Houston, BYU and Arizona this season, and it'll be interesting to see how it fares against the country's best competition outside the Big 12 with a national championship on the line.

It's a feat in of itself to go undefeated, which Utah can claim for the regular season with a win over West Virginia.

Not only did quarterback Ty Dieffenbach go down with an injury against Michigan, but the Bruins were also upset. If Dieffenbach is to miss UCLA's upcoming game against crosstown rival Southern California, it could be in trouble.

Dieffenbach could potentially return to face the Trojans , which will be a tough game regardless in a virtual must-win scenario. A 10-2 finish for the Bruins could potentially leave them out of the CFP, based on how the final rankings shake out.

UCLA still controls its own destiny, but has to beat USC in a huge game.

Unlike UCLA, Indiana might not control its own destiny. The Hoosiers' best win is against USC, and they might not reach the Big Ten championship game, which will leave Indiana's resume to be compared against other back end at-large teams vying for CFP berths.

Indiana has been plagued by poor recent quarterback play between Josh Hoover and Grant Wilson and its kickers have struggled, too. It's clear third-year coach Curt Cignetti doesn't have quite the same team he did last year after leading the Hoosiers to a national championship.

Kentucky was on pace for a magical season under first-year coach Will Stein earlier this season, but has since dropped three straight games against Tennessee, Florida and Missouri.

A win over in-state rival Louisville would be an exclamation point on an otherwise successful first season for the Wildcats, although the expectations had risen after their 7-1 start. Kentucky is trending up as a program, but trending down the last few weeks after its recent performances.
